title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) to evaluate whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases oracle pass rates for LLM‑produced NetOps configurations on vendor‑diverse emulated intent→configuration tasks. The frozen design used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics, declared model gpt‑5‑mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution completed 200 paired tasks (400 episodes) with model_calls_used=200. Results: baseline = 200/200 oracle passes; guarded = 200/200 oracle passes; absolute paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. The_null result is design‑bound: the shared initial candidate passed the deterministic oracle in every pair, so the repair stage was never exercised (repair_calls_invoked = 0). We publish the full artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) and provide artifact‑anchored recommendations (independent generation semantics, calibrated difficulty, larger repair budgets) for informative follow‑ups.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs promise to simplify intent‑driven NetOps by translating high‑level operator intent into low‑level device configuration. However, plausibly correct LLM outputs can still violate operational safety or policy (e.g., transiently breaking redundancy, touching protected interfaces, or violating ordered sequences). A common mitigation is a generate→validate→repair architecture: a generator proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic validator (oracle) checks objective properties in emulation, and a repair step attempts targeted correction when the oracle fails. Prior work demonstrates gains from constraint‑guided generation and verifier‑grounded repair in select settings, but reproducible, preregistered, artifact‑anchored confirmatory comparisons remain rare. We preregistered study‑cnd‑2026‑001 to measure the verifier benefit on a concrete operational estimand: the paired absolute difference in oracle pass rate when using a verifier‑assisted repair path versus unconstrained generation.

Research question and contributions. Research question: Does an automated verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increase the oracle pass rate (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) relative to unconstrained LLM generation across a preregistered set of 200 emulated intent→configuration tasks? Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered, autonomously executed, and fully archived paired evaluation (preregistration SHA‑256 a8969ac0...; initial master prompt provenance at provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 1872df1e...); (2) transparent, artifact‑anchored statistical inference (paired bootstrap and exact McNemar) showing no observed improvement under the frozen design and explaining the design cause; (3) deterministic reconciliation and per‑file SHA‑256 manifests that permit reproducible audit; (4) concrete, artifact‑grounded recommendations for experimental variants that will permit repairs to be exercised and measured.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑assisted and constraint‑guided approaches have appeared across NetOps and AIOps literature. Representative, verified works that motivated our preregistration include MeshAgent (constraint‑compiled guidance for network management), NetConfEval (intent→configuration benchmark design), and verifier‑grounded repair studies (e.g., StruSpec in program‑repair domains). These sources (cited_record_ids) influenced our choice to freeze a deterministic validator and to preregister a strict paired estimand. Unlike many prior reports, our design focused on preregistration, deterministic emulation, and per‑artifact hashing to enable full auditability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen plan. We froze the full scientific design before any final model calls (study id study‑cnd‑2026‑001; preregistration SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b...). The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1 (paired bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples, seed=1729, and exact McNemar two‑sided test). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one generator call per pair; the shared candidate supplied to both conditions), model = gpt‑5‑mini, validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. The full preregistration fields, sampling plan, and stopping rules are archived in the artifact bundle.

Task bank and stratification. The confirmatory sample comprised Npairs = 200, stratified by protocol: BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN = 50 pairs each. Within each protocol, vendor allocation was Cisco=17, Juniper=17, Arista=16 (totals Cisco=68, Juniper=68, Arista=64). Complexity was balanced (simple=100, complex=100). Each task manifest entry encodes: intent text, explicit initial and expected final states, required_sequence constraints, difficulty metadata, and a reference_answer (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl and representative artifacts, e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001‑baseline.json SHA‑256 eaf96aec...).

Generation, validation and repair. The run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter with declared generator gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 1acce925...). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the system performed one generator call per pair (model_calls_used = 200) and provided the identical candidate to both baseline and guarded scorers. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) executes an emulated, deterministic reachability and state simulation of the candidate and returns a normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, validator boolean valid, violation codes, and a validator trace. Repairs were permitted by preregistration but, in this run, never invoked (repair_applied = false across validator traces; repair_calls_invoked = 0). All raw outputs, provider traces, and validator traces were archived and SHA‑256 hashed (execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes (artifact‑anchored). The run completed 400 episodes (200 pairs), with 200 generator calls (shared candidates). Per‑pair scoring JSONs and provider traces are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/provider_calls/ with per‑file SHA‑256 digests. Aggregate scoring (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 1cb072b4...) reports: baseline_success_count = 200/200 (100%); guarded_success_count = 200/200 (100%). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...) is: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0.

Confirmatory inference. Using the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1: paired estimate = 0.00; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); exact McNemar two‑sided test p = 1.00. The analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 940b48e7...) and the deterministic reconciliation artifact (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 799b23b9...) provide the exact numbers and confirm internal accounting.

Representative exemplar. execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 eaf96aec...) illustrates a typical pair: the shared generated candidate matched the reference ordering for a medium difficulty intent (shutdown_configure_restore). The validator parsed 4 commands, simulated the emulated final state and returned valid = true and repair_applied = false. Similar validator traces exist for every archived pair (see execution/scoring/task-0000XX‑{baseline,guarded}.json files).
sections.discussion:
Why the observed null is design‑bound. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate generation semantics produced a single generated candidate per pair that both baseline and guarded conditions consumed. In every pair that shared candidate satisfied the deterministic oracle; therefore the repair pathway was never invoked (repair_calls_invoked = 0). Under this condition both arms necessarily yield identical pass/fail outcomes, producing n11 = 200 and no discordance. The inferential machinery (bootstrap and McNemar) correctly reports a point estimate of zero and degenerate CI [0.00,0.00]. Thus the result answers the preregistered estimand given the frozen design but does not measure the practical efficacy of repairs in regimes where initial candidates sometimes fail.

Implications for experimental design in verifier research. Two preregistered levers determine whether repairs can be exercised: (1) generation semantics (shared vs independent per condition) and (2) task/intent difficulty relative to generator capability. To measure repair value, the system must allow independent generator variance or tasks calibrated so that some initial candidates fail the validator. The archived artifacts document exactly how to implement both variants (change generation_semantics to independent_per_condition in a new preregistration; or augment execution/task_manifest.jsonl with higher difficulty seeds). The artifact hashes permit exact re‑launch of the same seed bank under alternate generation semantics.

Threats to validity and auditability. Internal validity: deterministic generation semantics and single declared model limit internal generality; we preserved preregistered exclusion and missingness rules (no provider drift occurred). Construct validity: the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces objective, emulation‑based properties (reachability, protected interfaces, required sequences) but may leave semantic blind spots; validator traces include per‑pair evidence of which predicates were exercised (execution/scoring/*.json). External validity: single model and emulation limit production generalization. Reproducibility and audit: every prompt, model call, provider trace, raw response, validator trace, scoring file, and analysis artifact is archived with per‑file SHA‑256; deterministic_reconciliation.json documents per‑stage counts and confirms consistency.

Actionable, artifact‑grounded follow‑ups. The archived bundle supports direct replication and immediate informative variants: (A) independent_per_condition generation (one generator call per condition per pair) — expected model_calls ~ 400; (B) calibrated difficulty: append higher‑difficulty tasks or adversarial border cases to the task manifest so some initial candidates fail the validator; (C) increase repair budget (>1 call/task) or enable iterative repair loops; (D) replicate across multiple generator models to assess generality. All new runs can reuse the same validator and scoring pipeline and will be auditable via per‑file SHA‑256 hashing.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed an auditable paired emulation assessment of a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair architecture under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Both baseline and guarded conditions passed the deterministic oracle on all 200 paired tasks; repairs were never called and the paired difference was 0.00 (95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p = 1.00). The null result is the expected consequence of the preregistered shared generation semantics combined with generator capability relative to the chosen task bank. The study demonstrates the critical role of generation semantics and task difficulty in allowing repairs to be exercised and measured. We release the full artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 digests) and provide concrete artifact‑grounded recommendations for follow‑up experiments that will permit meaningful measurement of verifier and repair benefits.

- Preregistration (frozen): study id = study-cnd-2026-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2. The preregistration froze the primary hypothesis, sampling plan, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared model, validator, repair budget, stopping rules, and analysis executor. The full preregistration artifact is archived in the execution bundle referenced in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- LLM and adapter: declared generator = gpt‑5‑mini executed via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model configuration artifact: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). All provider call traces and raw responses are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/ with per‑file SHA‑256 digests recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json (example provider trace: execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json SHA‑256 2e842c45...).
- Generation semantics (frozen): shared_initial_candidate (one generated candidate per pair, provided to both baseline and guarded conditions). This preregistered choice produced model_calls_used = 200 (one shared generation per 200 pairs) and is the proximate cause the repair stage was not invoked (repair_calls_invoked = 0). The execution manifest records these counts and per‑file hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json; raw results hash f51ee54d...).
- Validator and oracle: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored every candidate; representative scoring artifact: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 eaf96aec12c30860...). The validator is deterministic and emulation‑based (reachability, protected interfaces, required sequences); validator traces include parsed_command_count, normalized_configuration, validation predicates exercised, and repair_applied flags.
- Repair policy and budgeting: preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; in this run repair calls invoked = 0 (repair_applied = false in every validator trace). Had repairs been invoked, repair provider traces and repair_prompt SHA‑256 values would be archived similarly.
- Analysis procedures (frozen): paired_binary_analysis_v1 executed paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. Confirmatory analysis artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a42b5...), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 1cb072b4db7c...), analysis/results.json. The analysis log is archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 940b48e7...).
- Execution and reproducibility: every prompt, model output, provider trace, validator trace, scoring record, manifest and analysis artifact is archived with SHA‑256 digests. Deterministic reconciliation confirms arithmetic and accounting consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 799b23b9...).
- Human involvement: pre‑lock collaborative development (topic selection, infrastructure rehearsal) occurred; after the autonomy lock no human performed manual substantive editing of the scientific content reported here. Pre‑lock artifacts were not used as evidence unless reproduced under the frozen post‑lock workflow.
- Deviations: none affecting the primary confirmatory analysis; model identifier did not change mid‑run; no pairs were excluded. The key design choice (shared_initial_candidate) produced the observed ceiling effect; this is fully disclosed and artifact‑anchored.
limitations: Confirmatory conclusions apply only to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, single declared model gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic/emulated task bank of 200 pairs).

Shared_initial_candidate execution semantics created a ceiling effect: because the shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle for every task, the repair stage was never invoked (repair_calls_invoked = 0), preventing measurement of repair utility in this run.

Emulation with a deterministic validator and synthetic tasks does not capture full production heterogeneity (real vendor images, nondeterministic device behavior, or longer multi‑step operational workflows).
Single‑model execution limits generality across model families and instruction‑tuning variants; multi‑model replication is an informative follow‑up.
Repair budget was intentionally limited (≤1 call/task) by preregistration; richer iterative repair strategies remain unexplored in this run.
Oracle blind spots (uncovered semantic failure modes) may remain despite deterministic validation; per‑pair validator coverage diagnostics are archived in scoring artifacts.
